bands.why: A reasonable dodger clears the first round almost every time; the bot reacts faster than a thumb.
The hardest round is hard, yet still winnable.
A round lasts about 10 to 40 seconds (ticks: 120 per second).
Standing still loses within 1 to 5 seconds: the chasers have teeth.
Random steering never collects ten sparks: where the thumb goes must matter.

notes: Real-time example (moves are ticks, 120 per second; the first-payoff window counts seconds). Three tuning rows on the 0..100 scale, sampled at their lower bounds (0/34/67). Proposed 2026-09-29 from the first sim run: the dodge player wins 1.0 / 0.7 / 0.33 of the three rounds, collects its first spark within a second (the opening puts it 150 units from the start), and the halo pulse throws chasers back about twice per round at d34. Standing still loses in under 3 seconds and random steering collects no sparks. Waiting for the owner's play-test.
